name: Anchor Hierarchy
summary: Color-coded icons, bookmarks, a component minimap, and hover shortcuts for a faster, more organized Hierarchy.
detail: A deeper Hierarchy window: color-coded icons per GameObject (Alt+Click any row to open the palette), a component minimap with a one-click mini-inspector, a bookmark bar for jumping across scenes, and hover shortcuts for toggling active state, framing, and expanding or isolating subtrees — no mouse required.

name: Anchor Inspector
summary: Organized inspectors from attributes, with no editor code: sections, tabs, conditions and buttons, plus bookmarks and component tools.
detail: A cleaner, faster Inspector. Mark a script with [SectionedInspector] and its headers become nested, foldable sections with badges and tooltips; tabs, conditions, buttons and callbacks work on any script. Every Inspector window also gets a navigation bar with history and bookmarks, buttons on component headers, a toolbar under asset titles, and searchable enum fields.

name: Anchor Project
summary: Custom icons and color-coding for Project window folders, so you can spot the right one at a glance.
detail: Custom icons and color-coding for Project window folders, built on the same palette system as Anchor Hierarchy — spot the right folder at a glance instead of reading labels one by one.

name: Anchor Quick Select
summary: Pin GameObjects, assets, and folders into named pages, with a persistent Shift+1–9 speed dial in one searchable panel.
detail: One searchable panel for everything you keep hunting for: bookmarks organized into named, reorderable pages, a Recent tab for jumping back to previous selections, and a persistent Shift+1–9 speed dial that binds to specific objects — per scene for GameObjects, by GUID for assets, so a binding survives renames and moves. Opens docked with Ctrl+Q or as a hold-to-peek overlay with Alt+Q. Bookmarks are shared with Anchor Hierarchy rather than kept as a second private list.

name: Anchor Validator
summary: Find what's broken, wasteful or unused in your project, and fix it with a preview first.
detail: One window that scans your project for what's broken, wasteful or unused — missing scripts, pink materials, buttons that silently stopped working, assets nothing uses — and says what each finding means and what each fix does. Missing scripts can be recovered with their saved values. Scans never change anything, fixes in open scenes use Undo, and deletes go to the system Trash.

name: Anchor PlayerPrefs
summary: See and edit PlayerPrefs live in Play Mode, with Undo, snapshots to compare and restore, a sandbox for every run, a log of every write, and the code using each key.
detail: Anchor PlayerPrefs lists your project’s PlayerPrefs with their types and values, and keeps them current while your game runs in Play Mode. Every edit is one Undo step. Snapshots save the whole store to compare and restore later, the sandbox puts it back after every Play session, and the Changes page records every write in order. Find in Code shows the lines of your scripts that use a key, and which keys no script uses anymore. Unity’s EditorPrefs open in the same window.

name: Anchor Renamer
summary: Batch-rename assets and GameObjects with stacked rules and a live preview. Swaps and case-only renames just work, and an asset batch can be undone even after an Editor restart.
detail: Anchor Renamer builds new names from a stack of rules, Override Name, Find & Replace, Prefix / Suffix, Format Case, Quick Cleanup, Trim Characters and Numbering, and shows the result for every asset or GameObject in a live preview before anything is written. Conflicts are marked and resolved with one click, swaps, cycles and case-only renames just work, and Undo Last Rename reverts an asset batch even after a recompile or an Editor restart. Five built-in presets cover the common cases, and your own stacks are available in every project.

name: Anchor 2D Ruler
summary: On-canvas distance, range, and FOV cone measurement for 2D scenes, with grid snapping and 1-click copy.
detail: A native UI Toolkit overlay for 2D measurement in Scene View. Four modes — line, path, box, and cone — cover distance, area, and FOV checks, with concentric range circles, magnetic and tilemap snapping, and 1-click clipboard copy on any measurement badge. A recent-measurements drawer keeps your last few copies within reach.
